intro_line: Manila: colonial walls, jeepney chaos, and bay sunsets.
intro: Manila rewards visitors who look past the traffic to find Intramuros, old Binondo, and a restless food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: LRT Line 1 (green) links Malate, Ermita, Quiapo, Binondo and Santa Cruz; most sights sit along it.
LRT Line 2 (blue) serves Quiapo, Sampaloc and Santa Mesa; trains are packed at rush hour.
City buses start around PHP 16 and provincial buses around PHP 12; route numbers are shown on the bus.
Jeepneys start around PHP 10 for the first 4 km; routes are painted on the sides, not numbered.
Grab, Angkas, Gojek, Joyride and MyTaxi.PH ride apps work; taxis are plentiful but insist on the meter.
Tricycles, pedicabs and calesa horse carriages cover short trips; a one-hour calesa ride costs around PHP 50-70.

airports.name: Ninoy Aquino International Airport
airports.note: Main international gateway, about 11 km south of the centre.
